newsitem.title: USA: Dean Witter quarter aided by credit services.
newsitem.headline: Dean Witter quarter aided by credit services.

text.p: Dean Witter, Discover & Co., reporting higher first-quarter results, said Thursday its earnings were aided by the strength of its credit card business.

The financial services and credit card company reported first-quarter profits of $276.3 million, or 81 cents a share, on revenues of $2.44 billion. A year earlier, it earned $245.8 million, or 71 cents a share, on revenues of $2.17 billion.
"In our credit card business, we benefited from the pricing actions we took last year in response to rising writeoffs," Chairman Philip Purcell said in a statement.
"In securities, we continued to achieve strong earnings and impressive growth in the number of account executives, new client accounts and assets under management."
The company said net operating revenues, or total revenues minus interest expense and the provision for loss on receivables, rose to $1.65 billion from $1.55 billion in the 1996 first quarter.
Dean Witter said credit services income rose to $146.2 million, up from $124.3 million in 1996.
Income from securities transactions rose to $130.1 million from $121.5 million for 1996.
"We're proud of the results and this has also been an historic quarter because of the announcement of our merger with Morgan Stanley (Group Inc.)," he added.
Earlier in April, the equity research departments of Morgan Stanley and Dean Witter combined, although the formal merger of the two firms, announced in February, is still pending.
Dean Witter stock was up 37.5 cents at $36.625 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
